AMARA.short: Amara, a beautiful 19-year-old illiterate girl, suffers under her wicked stepmother Mama Esther who stopped her school. When rich CEO Bright falls in love with her and teaches her to read, her jealous step-family tries to marry her off to a 62-year-old man. But Amara rises to become best graduating student and gets her revenge through forgiveness.
AMARA.long: After losing her mother at 8, Amara is removed from school by her wicked stepmother Mama Esther and turned into a house help while her stepsister Esther enjoys SHS and iPhone. At 19, she meets Bright, a 27-year-old rich and kind CEO who falls for her pure heart despite her being illiterate. He starts teaching her A-B-C every evening. Consumed by jealousy, Mama Esther tries to forcefully marry Amara to a 62-year-old drunkard for 2 goats. Bright and her father save her. Amara leaves home with one bag, enrolls in evening school, is mocked as the oldest in class, but studies for 3 years with no makeup, no party. On graduation day, she is named BEST GRADUATING STUDENT while her jealous step-family watches in tattered clothes. That same night Bright proposes, and at her big wedding, Amara forgives them. A story of jealousy, love, education and forgiveness.

AMARA.full:
### PART 1: HOW IT ALL STARTED

*SCENE 1*
Amara's mother dies. Little Amara 8 years crying on grave. Papa Amara broken. Mama Esther appears at funeral, acting nice, consoling Papa Amara. She has a plan already.

Voiceover: "When Amara lost her mother, Mama Esther saw an opportunity. Not to be a mother... but to be an owner."

*SCENE 2*
6 months later, Mama Esther moves in with Esther. First week she is nice. Second week, she removes Amara from school. She tells Papa Amara: "Why waste money? Girls will marry. Let Esther go, she is brilliant."

Papa Amara agrees. Amara stops in Primary 4. From then she becomes house help in her father's house.

*SCENE 3 - 11 YEARS OF HELL*
Amara now 19. She wakes 4am, sweeps, cooks, fetches water, goes to market. She cannot read price, market women cheat her. Esther, same age, goes to school, wears nice clothes, uses iPhone.

Jealousy dialogue: Esther: "Amara, read this letter for me na" - laughs - "Oh I forgot, you can't read. Illiterate!" Mama Esther joins: "Your mother gave birth to a house girl."

---

### PART 2: THE ARRIVAL OF BRIGHT

*SCENE 4*
Amara from the market, carrying heavy food stuffs. A man in his car spill water on Amara. A handsome man - BRIGHT. He owns biggest company's in the city.

Bright: "Hey, let me help you." He carries it. Amara is shy.

*SCENE 5*
Bright starts seeing her everyday. He notices she never goes to school. He writes his number on paper for her: "Call me if you need anything."

Amara holds paper upside down, tears in eyes: "I... I don't know how to read."

Bright is shocked. He understands everything instantly.

*SCENE 6*
Mama Esther and Esther see Bright dropping Amara home. Jealousy starts DEEPLY.

Mama Esther: "Look at this illiterate girl. She wants to snatch a rich CEO? Never!"
Esther: "Mummy, he is supposed to be mine! I'm the educated one! He can't marry a girl who can't write her name."

From that day, they increase wickedness. They lock food, beat her, tell Papa Amara that Amara is following men.

*SCENE 7*
Mama Esther tries to slap Amara for talking to Bright. Bright appears at the gate at that exact time and holds Mama Esther's hand.

Bright (angry for first time): "Don't you ever touch her again! If you want to fight, fight me!"

Papa Amara sees this. For first time, he sees Mama Esther's real face. Amara runs and hugs Bright, crying.

---

### PART 3: LOVE AND EDUCATION

*SCENE 8*
Bright takes Amara to a coffee shop. He says: "I love you not because you can read, but because your heart is pure. But I will help you read."

Every evening 7pm - 9pm after work, he teaches her A-B-C. Amara cries, struggles, but learns fast because she is hungry for knowledge.

Mama Esther sends people to spy on them, telling village people Amara is now a bad girl sleeping in a man's house.

*SCENE 9*
Mama Esther's FINAL WICKED PLAN. She arranges marriage for Amara to a 62-year-old drunkard man in village for 2 goats and money, without Papa Amara knowing.

The old man comes to pick Amara one morning. Amara screams. Esther is videoing and laughing.

Bright arrives with police and Papa Amara. Papa Amara shouts: "Over my dead body! No one marries off my daughter!"

Papa Amara finally chases Mama Esther out of his bedroom and tells her to stay in visitors room.

That night, Papa Amara tells Amara: "My daughter, forgive me. Go with Bright. Go and be what your mother wanted you to be."

Amara leaves home with one bag.

*SCENE 10*
Amara enrolls in Adult Evening School. She is the oldest in SHS 1 class. Students laugh. Teachers pity her. She fails first exams. She wants to quit.

Bright every day: Buys her books, cooks for her, waits outside school in rain. He tells her: "The girl they called illiterate will graduate one day."

She reads all night. For 3 years, no party, no makeup, only books.

Mama Esther and Esther keep coming to school to mock her: "See illiterate girl wearing uniform!"

---

### PART 4: THE PAYBACK - GRADUATION & WEDDING

*SCENE 11 - GRADUATION DAY*
Big hall. Name is called: "AMARA OWUSU - BEST GRADUATING STUDENT, ARTS DEPARTMENT!"

Amara walks in graduation gown, glowing, confident, speaks fluent English. Everyone stands and claps. Papa Amara in wheelchair crying, Bright filming with proud smile.

Outside the gate, Mama Esther and Esther watching from far, wearing old clothes. Esther couldn't even pass WASSCE. Jealousy is eating them alive. Esther cries: "Mummy, that should have been me!"

*SCENE 12 - THE PROPOSAL*
Same night after graduation, Bright takes Amara to his house, decorated with flowers. He kneels down.

Bright: "Amara, I met you when you couldn't write your name. Today you are a graduate. Will you marry me?"

Amara cries and says YES.

*SCENE 13 - THE WEDDING*
Big Ghanaian traditional wedding + white wedding. Amara is stunning. Bright is handsome. Papa Amara gives her away, healthy now.

Mama Esther and Esther come late, not invited, in tattered clothes, to beg. They kneel before Amara.

Mama Esther: "Amara, forgive us. We were wicked. We tried to destroy you because of jealousy."

Esther: "Sister, please forgive me. I mocked you. Now I have nothing."

Amara, in her wedding gown, lifts them up and hugs them.

Amara: "I forgave you long time ago. If you didn't keep me illiterate, I would never have met Bright who taught me. Your wickedness led me to my destiny."

Everyone cries. Bright hugs Amara.

*FINAL TEXT ON SCREEN:* "They tried to keep her down because of jealousy, but God lifted her up. Forgiveness is the final victory."

THE ABANDONED HUTS.short: Handsome city boy Emmanuel returns to Amedzofe, Ghana's highest village in the clouds, after 15 years to find 3 abandoned huts at the edge of the Amedzofe forest. Everyone in Amedzofe is scared of Maame Serwaa who vanished in mist 40 years ago. But the truth will make you cry.
THE ABANDONED HUTS.long: THE ABANDONED HUTS - The Vanishing of Maame Serwaa is a Ghanaian folktale from Amedzofe Village, Volta Region, Ghana's highest human settlement at 677 meters above sea level. Amedzofe is located north of Ho in Ho West District, at the foot of Mount Gemi, famous for Ote Falls, cold misty weather and Dark Forest Egemese. Emmanuel, a handsome young man from Accra, returns to his grandfather's village in Amedzofe after 15 years in the city. He finds 3 abandoned huts covered in bush that no one in Amedzofe enters. An old man with a walking stick, Papa Kwasi, 87 years, tells him the true story of Maame Serwaa, the kindest old woman of Amedzofe who had 3 huts for cooking, sleeping and healing, and who vanished one rainy night in the Amedzofe mist 40 years ago leaving only her wrapper. Villagers of Amedzofe say the huts are cursed. But when Emmanuel follows a singing voice at night into the Amedzofe Dark Forest, he discovers Maame Serwaa is alive in the mist, and the real reason she vanished will break your heart. Tales By Zeenat Netflix Original set in Amedzofe, Volta Region.
THE ABANDONED HUTS.full:
NARRATOR: At the edge of Amedzofe village, the highest human settlement in Ghana at 677 meters, where clouds touch the roofs every morning at the foot of Mount Gemi. 3 old huts stand covered in bush near the Dark Forest Egemese. The thick mist from Amedzofe mountains covers them. No one in Amedzofe goes there.

EMMANUEL: [Handsome, white shirt, clean jeans, watch, from Accra, returns to Amedzofe after 15 years] Wow, Amedzofe changed! Cold like this! But what are those 3 huts there at edge of Amedzofe forest near Ote Falls side?

CHILDREN: Don't go! Maame Serwaa place in Amedzofe! If you go you won't come back! The Dark Forest will take you!

PAPA KWASI: [87 years, walking stick, brown smock, cap, oldest man in Amedzofe] You looking at the huts, city boy? Tap tap tap. You have your grandfather Kofi's stubborn face. You came from Accra to Amedzofe. Sit. You want to know why we in Amedzofe are scared? I will tell you.

NARRATOR: Flashback 40 years ago in Amedzofe.

PAPA KWASI: Maame Serwaa was the kindest old woman in Amedzofe, Volta Region. 3 huts - one for cooking for whole Amedzofe, one for sleeping, one for herbs from Mount Gemi that healed our children. When woman dey in labour in Amedzofe, we call Maame Serwaa. When pikin get fever from cold, we run to Maame Serwaa.

VILLAGER WOMAN: Why everyone in Amedzofe loves her? She must be witch! She is too kind, something dey inside!

NARRATOR: One rainy night in Amedzofe, thunder on Mount Gemi. Maame Serwaa went to her 3 huts singing her Ewe lullaby.

VILLAGERS: [Morning in Amedzofe, shouting in mist] Maame Serwaa! Maame Serwaa! She is gone! Only her wrapper on ground near the huts!

PAPA KWASI: For 40 years, empty. Since then, if you enter those 3 huts in Amedzofe, you hear crying at night. Yaw from Ho entered in 1998 to prove brave and ran mad for 3 days. So we chiefs of Amedzofe put rule: No one goes to the 3 huts. We abandoned them near Dark Forest.

EMMANUEL: [Laughs] Papa Kwasi, you Amedzofe old people and stories! Ghost in mist? This is 2026, not 1960!

PAPA KWASI: [Angry, hits stick on Amedzofe stone] You city boys think you know everything because you wear white shirt from Accra! You think we in Amedzofe are fools? Go then! Go tonight and see Amedzofe spirits!

NARRATOR: Night in Amedzofe. 11:47 PM. Cold 19 degrees. Mist 10 meters visibility. Emmanuel can't sleep in his grandfather house. The whole Amedzofe is silent except waterfall sound from Ote Falls. Then - he hears it. Old woman singing Ewe lullaby. From direction of 3 huts near Dark Forest.

EMMANUEL: [Torch shaking, walking through Amedzofe bush] Who is singing in this Amedzofe mist? Hello? Is someone there near the huts?

NARRATOR: First hut empty. Second hut mortar and pestle still there. Third hut - his torch freezes. Maame Serwaa is there, back to him, singing lullaby she used to sing for Amedzofe children 40 years ago. Her cloth blue and yellow kente clean, not old.

MAAME SERWAA: [Old woman, white hair, blue and yellow kente, turns slowly, tears not anger, face with tribal marks] You are Kofi's grandson from Accra who returned to Amedzofe. You have his eyes.

EMMANUEL: [Drops torch in Amedzofe mud] You... you are alive? For 40 years Amedzofe said you are ghost in mist!

MAAME SERWAA: I never died, my son. I vanished in Amedzofe mist. They called me witch in Amedzofe because I was kind. That rainy night 40 years ago, jealous women of Amedzofe came with cutlasses to burn my 3 huts, shouting witch. I heard them coming from Mount Gemi side. If I stayed, men of Amedzofe would fight to protect me, and blood would spill in Amedzofe because of me. My kindness would cause murder in this highest village. So I walked into Amedzofe forest mist, into Egemese Dark Forest, singing loudly so they think spirits took me. I left my wrapper on purpose on Amedzofe ground. For 40 years I live deep in Amedzofe forest behind Ote Falls, but every night I come back quietly to leave herbs at edge of huts for sick children of Amedzofe. The crying you hear in huts is me crying for my Amedzofe village.

NARRATOR: Behind Emmanuel, Papa Kwasi appears with Amedzofe villagers holding lanterns, shaking in cold Amedzofe mist, scared.

PAPA KWASI: [Falls to knees on Amedzofe mountain stone, crying first time in 40 years] Maame Serwaa! Forgive us! Forgive me! People of Amedzofe forgive me! It was me! I started rumor in Amedzofe! I was young and jealous! Everyone in Amedzofe came to you, not to me the elder! I brought them that night to burn your 3 huts! You vanished because of me! Amedzofe lost you because of me!

VILLAGERS: [Gasp in Amedzofe Ewe language] Ei! Papa Kwasi!

MAAME SERWAA: [Touches Papa Kwasi head, blessing] My son, I forgave you the night I left Amedzofe in mist.

NARRATOR: Thick white mist rolls from Mount Gemi, from Ote Falls side, covers 3 huts of Amedzofe. Soft, warm, not scary. Maame Serwaa walks towards her huts.

MAAME SERWAA: Don't let Amedzofe abandon kindness again.

NARRATOR: She steps into Amedzofe mist, slowly vanishes like mother returning to sleep in clouds. Her wrapper floats in Amedzofe cold air and lands gently in Emmanuel's hands. Mist clears over Mount Gemi. 3 huts of Amedzofe suddenly don't look scary. They look like home. All Amedzofe villagers crying, not from fear.

EMMANUEL: [One month later in Amedzofe, rebuilding with Amedzofe youth] I am not going back to Accra. I will stay in Amedzofe.

NARRATOR: Emmanuel uses city money to rebuild 3 Abandoned Huts of Amedzofe exactly as they were, but with new meaning for Volta Region: HUT 1: MAAME SERWAA COMMUNITY CLINIC OF AMEDZOFE - Free for pregnant women and children of Ho West. HUT 2: STORY HUT OF AMEDZOFE - Where Papa Kwasi sits every evening with stick to tell TRUE story of Amedzofe to tourists who climb Mount Gemi. HUT 3: HERB HUT - With wood carving: MAAME SERWAA - THE WOMAN WHO VANISHED IN AMEDZOFE MIST TO SAVE US. Tourists who visit Ote Falls and Gemi Mountain now visit huts.

NARRATOR: Papa Kwasi, 87, no longer uses stick to walk in Amedzofe hills - he uses it to point at children and tourists and say this is where kindness lives in highest village in Ghana. At night, sometimes, if you pass huts near Dark Forest in Amedzofe, you still hear old woman singing lullaby in mist at 677 meters high. But now, no child in Amedzofe runs. They smile and sing along with Maame Serwaa. Some secrets vanish in Amedzofe mist, but kindness never does. END OF AMEDZOFE.

ANANSE AND THE VILLAGE THAT NEVER SLEPT.t: ANANSE AND THE VILLAGE THAT NEVER SLEPT
ANANSE AND THE VILLAGE THAT NEVER SLEPT.short: Akokrom village near Kumasi cursed to never sleep. No child, no goat can sleep. Kwaku Ananse the clever spider man comes to trick sleep back. A funny Ashanti folktale.
ANANSE AND THE VILLAGE THAT NEVER SLEPT.long: Long ago in Ashanti Region near Kumasi, there was a village called Akokrom. Happy village but one big problem - no one could sleep at night. Children cried, old men tired, farmers no rest. The chief promised 2 fat goats and gold dust. Ananse the spider man came to bring sleep back with a clever trick.
ANANSE AND THE VILLAGE THAT NEVER SLEPT.full:
NARRATOR: Long, long ago, in the Ashanti Region, not far from Kumasi, there was a village called Akokrom.

NARRATOR: Akokrom was a happy village, but they had one big problem. No one could sleep at night. Not because of noise. Not because of mosquitoes. But because the village was cursed to always be awake.

NARRATOR: Every night, when the sun set, the people of Akokrom would lie on their mats, close their eyes, but sleep would not come. Their eyes stayed open till morning. Children cried, old men were tired, farmers went to farm without rest.

CHIEF OF AKOKROM: Who can bring sleep back to our village?

NARRATOR: One day, Kwaku Ananse, the clever spider man, heard about it. He was not from Akokrom, but he heard that the chief promised 2 fat goats and a bag of gold dust to anyone who could bring sleep.

KWAKU ANANSE: Sleep? That is easy! I will trick sleep and bring it here.

NARRATOR: Ananse packed his small bag and walked to Akokrom. When he arrived, the village looked tired. Even the goats were awake!

KWAKU ANANSE: Nana, I can bring sleep back in 3 days. But I need one night alone in the village square.

CHIEF OF AKOKROM: I agree. You can have the square.

NARRATOR: That night, Ananse went to the square with a big drum. He started drumming. Gbo gbo gbo! He sang.

KWAKU ANANSE: Sleep, sleep, come to Akokrom, we are tired, we want to sleep. Sleep, sleep, come to Akokrom!

NARRATOR: All the villagers came out. They were surprised. Then Ananse did something clever. He brought a pot of palm wine and poured it on the ground.

KWAKU ANANSE: This is for Asaase Yaa, Mother Earth! We have offended the earth, that is why she took our sleep! For years, you have been making noise at night, fighting, playing drums till midnight. You never let the earth rest. So the earth also took your rest!

OLD MEN: It is true! Akokrom has become a noisy village. Every night there is a party, a fight, or loud drums.

KWAKU ANANSE: Tonight, no one will talk. No one will drum. We will all sit in silence from 7pm to 5am. We will show respect to the night.

NARRATOR: That night, for the first time in many months, Akokrom was quiet. No talking. No drumming. Only the crickets.

NARRATOR: And slowly, something happened. Little Ama, the 6-year-old, closed her eyes... and slept! Then her mother slept. Then the chief slept. One by one, the whole village fell into deep, sweet sleep. Krr krr - snoring filled the air!

VILLAGERS: We have slept! We have slept! Ananse is wise!

CHIEF OF AKOKROM: Thank you Ananse! Here are your 2 fat goats and a bag of gold dust!

KWAKU ANANSE: I did not bring sleep with magic. Sleep was always here. You just chased it away with noise and worry. When you respect the night, the night will respect you. Every night after 8pm, let your village sleep. No loud noise, no quarrel. Then sleep will never leave you again.

NARRATOR: And till today, the people of Akokrom sleep early and wake strong.

NARRATOR: MORAL: Respect the night and your body. Sleep is not bought with money, it comes with peace. END.

THE RIVER BRIDE.short: A beautiful 19-year-old village girl is chosen as a bride for the River God to save her village from drought. But she loves a hunter. Now she must choose - marry a god for water, or die for love.
THE RIVER BRIDE.long:
THE RIVER BRIDE is a powerful Ghanaian folklore about love, sacrifice, and the spirits of the river.

In a small village called Umunzu near River Niger, rain has not fallen for seven months. Farms are dry and children are crying. The elders say the river demands a bride.

19-year-old Adaeze, daughter of poor farmer Obinna, is chosen. She loves Emeka the hunter, but to save her village she must marry the River God.

What will happen when she becomes River Bride? Will Emeka wait for her? Will Mamala the first wife of River God kill her? This is Part 1 of the River Bride Trilogy - clean Nigeria Normal English version.

THE RIVER BRIDE.full:
NARRATOR: In a small village called Umunzu, near River Niger, rain had not fallen for seven months. Farms were dry. Children were crying. The elders were afraid.

IGWE OKORO: Our river is angry! Who will save us?

ELDER OKAFOR: Igwe, the old priestess said it before — the river demands a bride. A pure girl to marry the water.

NARRATOR: In that village, there was a 19-year-old girl, Adaeze. She was very beautiful, kind, and the only child of a poor farmer. She was in love with Emeka, the hunter's son.

ADAEZE: Emeka, when will you come and marry me? My father is waiting.

EMEKA: Adaeze, I am gathering money. By the next market day, you will be my wife. I promise you.

IGWE OKORO: Our priestess has spoken. The river has chosen. A girl born on Saturday, with a mark on her left shoulder — she will be the River Bride, or we will all die.

PRIESTESS NNEKA: She is the one! Adaeze, daughter of Obinna! Tomorrow by midnight, you must go to the river with a white wrapper. The River God will come to take you.

OBINNA: My only child! No! Take my farm! Take my life!

ADAEZE: Father, if I don't go, the whole village will die of hunger.

EMEKA: Adaeze, I will not allow it! I will fight the River God!

NARRATOR: At midnight, Adaeze walked to the river alone. She wore a white wrapper and was crying. The water started spinning. A tall, handsome man came out from the water, his eyes shining like diamonds.

RIVER GOD: Adaeze... I have waited 100 years for you. You have finally come. Come and be my queen. Your village will have rain forever.

ADAEZE: I don't want to be a queen! I love Emeka! I am human!

RIVER GOD: Love? Human love dies in one year. Mine is forever. If you refuse me, your village will become a desert for seven years.

EMEKA: Leave her! She is mine!

NARRATOR: Emeka attacked the River God, but his cutlass just passed through water. The River God laughed.

RIVER GOD: Foolish boy! You cannot kill water!

RIVER GOD: I give you a choice, Adaeze. Marry me tonight, and I will give your village rain, and I will let this boy live. If you refuse, I will take you by force, and I will kill him and your father.

ADAEZE: If I become the river bride, will my people live?

RIVER GOD: They will prosper more than before. And you... you will never die. You will become a goddess.

ADAEZE: Tell my father that I love him. And tell the village... I did it for them.

EMEKA: ADAEZE!!!!

NARRATOR: Adaeze entered the river. The water closed. Immediately, heavy rain started falling! Thunder! The dry river started flowing full! People started dancing!

But deep inside the water, Adaeze did not die. She sat on a throne of gold and pearls. The River God placed a crown on her head.

RIVER GOD: You are now the River Bride. But you are sad.

ADAEZE: My heart is still on land.

RIVER GOD: I will give you power. Once every year, on the night you became my bride, you can return to land for one night as a human. But if you ever sleep with a human man that night, both of you will turn to river stones forever.

NARRATOR: One year later, that night came. Adaeze returned to land, beautiful and shining. Emeka was still waiting by the river side. He never married.

EMEKA: Adaeze? Is that you? You have come back!

ADAEZE: Emeka! I have only one night!

NARRATOR: They hugged, they cried, and they talked all night. Emeka wanted to touch her, but Adaeze told him about the curse. So they just held hands till morning.

Every year, Adaeze came. The village now worships her. They call her Mama Rain. Children bring white flowers for her.

But last year, something happened. Emeka has grown a little older, but Adaeze is still 19. And the River God has become jealous...

RIVER GOD: Adaeze, you love him more than me. This year, if you go to meet him, I will not let you return. You will die.

ADAEZE: Then let me die! I want one night to be a human wife, not a goddess!

NARRATOR: What will happen this year? Will Adaeze risk death to be with Emeka for one night? Will the River God destroy the village again?

TO BE CONTINUED IN RIVER BRIDE PART 2...

RIVER BRIDE PART 2 - THE LAST NIGHT.short: One year later, Adaeze risks everything to be a human wife for one night. But Mamala the first wife wants to kill her, Amara wants Emeka, and little Zara is dying. Will love survive?
RIVER BRIDE PART 2 - THE LAST NIGHT.long:
RIVER BRIDE PART 2 - THE LAST NIGHT is the powerful continuation of the Ghanaian folklore epic.

Adaeze is now River Bride goddess. She gets one night every year to be human. This anniversary night she wants to be wife to Emeka the hunter who has waited 2 years.

But inside the river, Mamala the jealous first wife with snakes in her hair plans to drown them. On land, Amara loves Emeka secretly and follows them. And 7-year-old Zara is sick by the river crying for help.

Adaeze heals Zara with her goddess power and breaks river law, becomes weak. Mamala attacks! Will Ngozi mother spirit save her? Will River God King forgive her pure heart?

Clean Nigeria Normal English, full story with all 12 characters. Part 3 THE FINAL END 2026 is the final war!

RIVER BRIDE PART 2 - THE LAST NIGHT.full:
SYNOPSIS:* One year later, Adaeze wants to risk everything to be a human wife for one night. But the River God's first wife, Mamala, wants to kill her, Amara wants to steal Emeka, and little Zara is dying.

*FULL STORY:*

*NARRATOR:* It was the anniversary night. The night Adaeze became the River Bride. Inside the river palace, Adaeze sat on her throne, crying. Her crown was heavy.

*RIVER GOD:* Adaeze, you are crying again. Tonight you can go to land. But I warned you. If you go to see that boy, I will not allow you to come back. You will die as a human.

*ADAEZE:* Then let me die. I don't want to be a goddess forever. I want to be a wife for one night.

*NARRATOR:* Inside the deeper part of the river, someone was listening. It was MAMALA, the first wife of the River God. She was very beautiful, but her heart was full of jealousy.

*MAMALA:* (Angry) So this small human girl wants to leave our world? Good. Tonight, I will make sure she never returns. I will drown her boyfriend and kill her.

*NARRATOR:* On land, in Umunzu village, Emeka was waiting by the river. He had not married for two years. His best friend, OKONKWO, came to meet him.

*OKONKWO:* Emeka, my brother, you are here again? It is midnight. This girl is now a goddess. Forget her.

*EMEKA:* I can never forget her, Okonkwo. She said she would come every year. I will wait.

*OKONKWO:* And what about AMARA? That girl loves you. She brings you food every day. She is a good girl.

*EMEKA:* My heart belongs to Adaeze only.

*NARRATOR:* In another part of the village, AMARA was watching them from behind a tree. She was crying.

*AMARA:* Emeka, I have loved you for three years. Why can't you see me? Tonight, I will follow you to the river. I will make sure Adaeze leaves you alone.

*NARRATOR:* At midnight, the water began to spin. Adaeze came out, wearing her white wrapper, shining like moonlight. She was still 19.

*EMEKA:* Adaeze! You came!

*ADAEZE:* Emeka!

*NARRATOR:* They hugged. But before they could talk, they heard a small voice crying. It was LITTLE ZARA, the 7-year-old girl, coughing near the river bank.

*ADAEZE:* Zara? What are you doing here at night? You are burning with fever!

*LITTLE ZARA:* Mama Adaeze, I am sick. My mother said only the river goddess can save me. Please help me.

*ADAEZE:* Oh no. River God said if I touch any human tonight, I will lose my powers.

*EMEKA:* We must save her, Adaeze.

*ADAEZE:* (Touches Zara's head and prays) River, please heal this child.

*NARRATOR:* Immediately, Zara's fever disappeared. But inside the river, MAMALA felt it.

*MAMALA:* She used her power on land! Now she is weak! This is my chance.

*NARRATOR:* Suddenly, the river became rough. A big wave came out. MAMALA appeared, with snakes in her hair.

*MAMALA:* Adaeze! You are a selfish bride! You healed a human child without permission! You have broken the river law! Now you must die!

*ADAEZE:* Who are you?

*MAMALA:* I am Mamala! The first wife! The queen before you came! Tonight, I will take your life and take your boyfriend!

*EMEKA:* Leave her alone!

*OKONKWO:* (Running with his cutlass) Emeka! What is happening?

*NARRATOR:* Mamala raised her hand and the water held Emeka and Okonkwo, so they could not move.

*MAMALA:* You cannot fight me, humans!

*NARRATOR:* Adaeze was afraid and weak. She was about to give up. Then, a soft light appeared on the water. It was a woman in white. It was NGOZI, Adaeze's mother who died many years ago.

*NGOZI:* Adaeze, my daughter.

*ADAEZE:* Mama? Mama! Is that you?

*NGOZI:* Yes, my child. I have been watching you from the world of spirits. You have a pure heart. You saved Zara. That is true love, not selfish love. The river loves a pure heart.

*MAMALA:* Ngozi! You cannot save her! She broke the law!

*NGOZI:* No, Mamala. She followed the highest law — love. River God! Come and see what your bride did!

*NARRATOR:* The RIVER GOD appeared, tall and shining. He saw Zara, now healed and smiling. He saw Emeka who still waited after two years. He saw Adaeze who risked her throne to save a child.

*RIVER GOD:* Mamala, leave them. Adaeze has shown me what human love means. It is not selfish. It gives.

*MAMALA:* But you promised me she would die if she went to land!

*RIVER GOD:* I was jealous. I was wrong. Adaeze, you saved a child. You did not use your night for yourself. For that, I will forgive you.

*ADAEZE:* Thank you, my lord.

*RIVER GOD:* Tonight, I give you a new gift. You can be human for one full night. No curse. You and Emeka can be husband and wife till morning. And little Zara will never be sick again.

*LITTLE ZARA:* Thank you, Mama Adaeze!

*NARRATOR:* Mamala was angry and disappeared into the deep water forever.

*NGOZI:* My daughter, I am proud of you. Be happy tonight. (Her spirit disappears)

*NARRATOR:* Amara, who was watching from the bush, saw everything. She started crying and left quietly. She understood that Emeka and Adaeze's love was true.

*AMARA:* I will find my own love. Let them be happy.

*NARRATOR:* That night, Adaeze and Emeka finally became husband and wife by the river side, under the moon. Okonkwo played music and Zara danced.

It was their last night as humans, but it was the most beautiful night in Umunzu.

But in the morning, Adaeze had to return to the river...
